G-F111.trick: Sensory adaptation = you stop feeling your socks, but you'd notice a pebble right away.
G-F111.tip: Receptors respond most to change. A steady harmless stimulus fades; a new one gets noticed.

G-F112.trick: Golgi TENDON organ = senses TENSION (both start with T). Muscle spindle = senses stretch/length.
G-F112.tip: Tension at the tendon = Golgi tendon organ. Length or stretch in the muscle belly = muscle spindle.

G-F113.trick: Referred pain = crossed phone lines: the brain blames the skin for the organ's call (heart attack → left arm).
G-F113.tip: Visceral and skin nerves share spinal pathways, so the brain mislabels where pain comes from.

G-F114.trick: Flavor = taste + smell. Hold your nose and an apple tastes like a potato.
G-F114.tip: Most "taste" complaints after a cold are really loss of smell. Taste buds can still sense sweet, salty, sour, bitter, umami.

G-F115.trick: Front of tongue: Facial (VII) = Flavor (taste); Trigeminal (V) = Touch.
G-F115.tip: Same body part, different senses, different nerves. Match the type of sensation to the cranial nerve.

G-F116.trick: Eustachian (auditory) tube = the ear's pressure valve to the back of the nose (nasopharynx). Pops when you yawn.
G-F116.tip: This tube explains why throat infections spread to the middle ear, especially in kids with short, flat tubes.

G-F117.trick: Hair cells = tiny microphones that turn wiggles into nerve signals.
G-F117.tip: Transduction in hearing happens at cochlear hair cells, which signal CN VIII (vestibulocochlear).

G-F118.trick: Semicircular canals = spinning ("circles for circling"); the cupula sways like seaweed in the fluid.
G-F118.tip: Rotation = cristae in the semicircular ducts. Tilt or straight-line motion = maculae in the utricle and saccule.

G-F119.trick: Aqueous = watery front fluid. POSTERIOR chamber = the tiny gap behind the iris but in front of the lens.
G-F119.tip: Aqueous humor fills both the anterior and posterior chambers. Vitreous humor fills the big space behind the lens.

G-F120.trick: Near vision: ciliary muscle Contracts → zonules go slack → lens gets Chubby (round).
G-F120.tip: Near focus = rounder lens. Far focus = ciliary muscle relaxes, zonules pull tight, lens flattens.

C-ch12-receptors.trick: TRANSduction = TRANSlating a stimulus (light, sound, pressure) into a nerve signal.
C-ch12-receptors.tip: Transduction happens at the receptor. Perception (knowing what it is) happens in the brain.

C-ch12-somatic.trick: PROPRIOception = knowing your own (proprio) position, like touching your nose with eyes closed.
C-ch12-somatic.tip: Proprioceptors include muscle spindles, Golgi tendon organs and joint receptors.

C-ch12-chemical.trick: OLFACTion = the OLFACTory nerve (CN I): "Oh, what's that smell?"
C-ch12-chemical.tip: Smell is the only sense that doesn't relay through the thalamus first.

C-ch12-ear.trick: AURicle = the AURal (ear) flap you can see; it funnels sound into the canal.
C-ch12-ear.tip: Sound path: auricle → ear canal → eardrum → ossicles (malleus, incus, stapes) → oval window.

C-ch12-hearing.trick: COCHLEA = snail shell (cochlea = snail) where hearing happens.
C-ch12-hearing.tip: Cochlea = hearing. Vestibule and semicircular canals = balance.

C-ch12-balance.trick: MACULA = Moving in a straight line or tilting (gravity). Crista = spinning.
C-ch12-balance.tip: Maculae sit in the utricle and saccule and sense head position and linear acceleration.

C-ch12-eye.trick: RETINA = the movie screen at the back of the eye, covered in rods and cones.
C-ch12-eye.tip: Eye tunics: fibrous (sclera, cornea), vascular (choroid, ciliary body, iris), neural (retina).

C-ch12-vision.trick: ACCOMMODATION = the lens accommodates (adjusts its shape) for near vs far.
C-ch12-vision.tip: Losing accommodation with age is presbyopia, which is why many adults over 40 need reading glasses.

C-ch12-phototransduction.trick: PHOTO-transduction = light (photo) changed into a nerve signal by rods and cones.
C-ch12-phototransduction.tip: Unusual fact: light HYPERpolarizes photoreceptors and reduces their transmitter release.
